<cr>During the summer and fall of 1942, the Germans and their allies advanced deep into southeastern Russia with the largest territorial gains of their invasion of the USSR. Now, they find themselves dangerously overextended and exhausted. However, the Soviets have been building reserve armies and reinforcing their forces along the Don and Volga. Recognising that the Germans are ill-prepared for continued offensive operations, Stavka has decided to conduct a number of counteroffensive operations around Stalingrad, breaking through the Axis lines, surrounding their enemy and then continuing west.<cr>If their Stalingrad forces are cut off, the Germans will be hard pressed to save them.

<cr>The capture of Leningrad is one of the three strategic goals of Operation Barbarossa and the main target of Army Group North. The German plan calls for capturing the city on the move, with the Fourth Panzer Group advancing to establish a supply line for the following infantry forces that will be needed to assault the city. The mobile forces must then cut the Soviet supply lines into the city, isolating the defenders. The German infantry must concentrate its strength for the assault on the city's fortifications.<cr>The Soviet forces must delay the German advance as long as possible, while constructing fortifications to defend the city and its supply lines.

<cr>The first half of 1942 has seen a series of Soviet offensives pushing the Germans back from Moscow. As a result, a salient has been formed along the front line in the direction of the capital. In an effort to destroy the German 9th Army, the Soviets plan to launch multiple coordinated thrusts from all sides against the Rzhev-Vyazma Salient. If successful, the attacking armies will link up and advance towards Smolensk, enveloping and destroying the remaining German forces.<cr>The 9th Army has limited forces and reinforcement is unlikely. The defenders plan to stand their ground, creating strong-points in the Salient's towns if the Soviets advance past them, causing problems for the Red Army in their rear areas.

<cr>With the start of Operation Barbarossa, in the southeastern part of the Eastern Front, Army Group South has the primary objective of conducting a concentric offensive west of the Dnieper River. With Ukraine and its capital of Kiev as primary objectives, the 1st Panzer Group, along with the 6th and 17th Armies are to prevent enemy forces from retreating eastwards and destroy them.<cr>Standing in their way are the Soviet 5th, 6th and 12th Armies. The Soviet plan involves the Southwestern Front to conduct the Kiev Strategic Defensive Operation. This plan calls for the Southwestern Front to withdraw all available forces to the old Stalin Line fortifications to defend the approaches to Kiev.

During the 2nd half of 1943 the US 8th AF continues its massive 1,000 bomber raids on German industries. Most significant are the August to December raids on the German aircraft industry. 5,092 tons of explosives are dropped on 14 targeted aircraft plants (mostly airframe plants). Production of single-engine fighters (Bf 109s and Fw 190s) drops by 45%.<cr>The Americans take heavy losses in their raid in August against Regensburg and Schweinfurt, losing 60 planes and 664 crewmen KIA or POW. A later attack of the ball bearing plants around Schweinfurt in October also causes heavy losses, with the Americans losing 60 aircraft with 600 crewmen KIA or POW. These losses amount to 25% of the attacking force. <cr><cr>- Target: Heavy Industry <cr>- Damage 100, Radius 55, Raids 1 <cr><cr>- Target: Airframe <cr>- Damage 100, Radius 50, Raids 1 <cr><cr>- Target: Railyard <cr>- Damage 100, Radius 50, Raids 1

On January 26, 1942, the first American forces arrive in Europe, landing in Northern Ireland. The 133rd Infantry Regiment of the 34th Infantry Division was the first United States Army unit sent to Europe in World War II. The first battalion arrived in Belfast, followed by the rest of the regiment in February. These units were designated as US Army Northern Ireland forces (or MAGNET forces). The 133rd and 168th Infantry Regiments trained in the peat bogs and performed border guard patrols between British North Ireland and the neutral Irish Free State.<cr>The American Eigth Air Force was activated and the VIII Bomber Command (VIII BC) was sent to England. On February 22nd, the VIII BC was established at RAF Daws Hill, in High Wycombe.

On March 28, 1942, the RAF sends a raid against the city of Luebeck in Northern Germany. The attack creates a firestorm that destroys over 80% of the city's historic medieval centre. Three of the centre's main churches and large parts of the built-up area are destroyed.<cr>Adolf Hitler is enraged by this and orders the Luftwaffe to respond with equivalent retaliation.<cr>In late April thru the end of May, the Luftwaffe conducts the Baedeker Blitz, a series of raids on popular tourist and historic British sites. The aim is to begin a 'tit-for-tat' exchange with the hope of forcing the RAF to reduce their actions. The name of these raids comes from a comment made at the time by a spokesman for the German Foreign Office:<cr>'We shall go out and bomb every building in Britain marked with three stars in the Baedeker Guide'<cr>The attempt is an abject failure. Due to the RAF's improved night fighter and radar capabilities, the Luftwaffe suffers unsustainable losses for minimal damage to the targeted cities. Nevertheless the raids result in over 1,600 civilian deaths and damage to tens of thousands of homes.<cr>Note Picture: Luebeck Cathedral burning after British air raid.
